facts.text: Encanto Village is the smallest urban village in Phoenix, covering only about 8 square miles yet packing a dense, lively community.
The Encanto Citizens Association, founded over forty years ago, was Phoenix’s first neighborhood group dedicated to preserving historic sites.
In 1984 the ECA helped get the Encanto‑Palmcroft neighborhood and Encanto Park listed on the National Register of Historic Places, with later boundary expansions in 1992 and 1994.
Four Valley Metro Rail stops—Thomas, Osborn, Indian School, and Campbell—serve Encanto Village, making it a key transit hub in central Phoenix.
Encanto Village’s core is the Park Central Mall, surrounded by historic districts that include the Arizona State Fairgrounds and the Veterans Memorial Coliseum.
The village’s name comes from the Spanish word for “magic,” reflecting the area’s early 20th‑century charm and colorful street life.
